name: Mhachaki
why_it_matters: The most-cited Naga ethnic-food address near the ISBT bypass — a wood-and-bamboo-and-stone structure built to feel like a traditional morung. Menu pairs smoked-pork momo and kokhü (sticky rice cake) with a coffee bar; an attached lounge runs live bands on selected evenings. Ranked #5 of 33 Kohima restaurants on Tripadvisor (4.8/5).
insider_tip: It's on the bypass, not in the main bazaar — 10 minutes by cab from MG Marg, and easier to access if you're driving in from Dimapur. Order the smoked-pork momo + kokhü combo; the coffee is genuinely the best in this part of town.
signature_address: Opp. ISBT, Bypass Rutsa, NH-29, Kohima 797001

name: Hotel Bamboo Shoot
why_it_matters: One of the oldest tribal-cuisine kitchens in Kohima, serving Lotha dishes since 1994 from a tiny old-NST-market spot opposite Domino's. Cited by MorungExpress as the address for 'wonderful Lotha dishes' — bamboo shoot pork, smoked beef, anishi — at thali prices, before pan-Naga restaurants made the cuisine touristy.
insider_tip: Open Mon-Sat 10am-7pm only — closed Sundays, and the kitchen runs out by mid-afternoon. Ask for whatever's been smoked that week; if anishi (yam-leaf cake) is on, order it — most pan-Naga places skip it.

name: Mom and I Cafe
why_it_matters: Owner Pelevotuo Solo grew up in his mother's galho restaurant and opened Mom and I Cafe in tribute — 'Mom' is the senior galho cook, 'I' is the cafe's modern Asian-Naga menu. Galho (a one-pot Naga rice porridge with smoked meat and herbs) is the headline dish; the kitchen also runs Taiwanese beef noodles for the millennial crowd.
insider_tip: Order the galho if you've never had it — it's the dish most tourist menus skip. The peppery fried rice is the locals' default lunch order. First-floor space, look for the United Traders building near KAK Store.
signature_address: 1st Floor, United Traders, near KAK Store, Kohima 797001
